# orchestration_start_tool

> Start a workflow pipeline from a template.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | `orchestration` |
| Callable | MCP clients; in-app @ai conversations; grantable to agents |
| Filter | `https://www.dsiloed.com/api/v1/mcp?tools=orchestration_start_tool` |

## Description

This is the description the server sends to the model, verbatim.

Start a workflow pipeline from a template. Creates a workflow execution
and begins the first stage automatically.

Use this when a user requests work that matches a workflow template
(e.g., a feature request triggers the SDLC pipeline).

The workflow will post status updates to the current conversation
as stages progress.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `template_name` | string | yes | Name of the workflow template to use (e.g., "SDLC Pipeline") |
| `name` | string | yes | A short name for this execution (e.g., "Rate Limiting Feature") |
| `feature_request` | string | yes | The user's request or input text. IMPORTANT: Include the COMPLETE text verbatim — do NOT summarize, truncate, or paraphrase. |
| `repo_path` | string | no | Server-side path to the repository (e.g., "/home/user/projects/my_app"). Only include if the user explicitly provided a path. If omitted, falls back to the template custom_fields repo_path, then the SiloLink projects_path config. |
| `base_branch` | string | no | Git branch to base work from (defaults to "main") |
| `cost_limit_dollars` | number | no | Per-run cost limit in DOLLARS (e.g. 60 for a $60 cap). Overrides the template default. Set this when the requester states a budget — don't silently inherit a template cap that contradicts their stated limit. |
| `work_item_type` | string | no | Optional. The EXISTING record this run is for, so every deliverable files against it: "project" (Project), "task" (Task), or "ticket" (BizTxnEvent — a customer ticket, e.g. the bug report a Bug Fix run works). Pass when the user names one; omit for an ad-hoc run (it then files under the run itself). One of: `project`, `task`, `ticket`. |
| `work_item_id` | integer | no | Numeric id of the work_item_type record. Required when work_item_type is set. |
| `repos` | array of string | no | Optional. For a MULTI-REPO run (a feature spanning more than one repository, e.g. backend + frontend), the list of repo KEYS from the tenant dev_team repos registry this run targets (e.g. ["backend", "frontend"]). Set ONLY when the user names the repos; omit otherwise — a single-repo run uses the default repo, and the planner can infer repo scope from the work. |
| `runbook_file_id` | integer | no | Optional. LlmFile id of a deploy/ops RUNBOOK to use for THIS run, overriding the pipeline's default runbook. Set ONLY when the user names a specific runbook (e.g. "use the Acme deploy runbook") — first resolve that name to its LlmFile id with list_llm_files_tool, then pass the id here. If the user does not mention a runbook, omit this and the template default runbook is used. |
| `inputs` | object | no | Optional. Structured values this template declares it needs (its custom_fields.input_schema), as a FLAT key→value object — e.g. {"valuation_cap":"$5,000,000","investor_meetings_goal":30}. Extract whatever the user already stated in their request and pass it here. If you omit a REQUIRED field, this tool returns needs_input listing the missing fields — ask the user for exactly those, then call the tool again with them filled in. |
| `approver_party_ids` | array of integer | no | Optional. Party ids designated to APPROVE this run's human gate(s) (Pillar P2 — explicit gate holders). Each is assigned the `approver` role on the execution at start, so they are in place before the first gate fires; when set, ONLY these parties may approve. Omit to let any authorized human approve. |
| `owning_team_id` | integer | no | Optional. Party id of the TEAM that owns this run (Pillar P2). When the pipeline has a `team_lead` approval gate, the gate resolves to THIS team's lead — so the run need not own a team Project. Pass the team's party id when the user names a team; ignored if it is not a same-tenant team. |
| `approver_assignments` | object | no | Optional. Per-gate, role-based approvers (Pillar P2) — a map of approver ROLE id → array of Party ids, e.g. {"underwriter":[12],"manager":[34]}. Use when a pipeline's gates declare DIFFERENT approver roles (its required_approver_roles); each named party is assigned that role on the run, so each gate resolves to its own holder(s). Unknown roles / foreign ids are ignored. For a single generic gate holder use approver_party_ids instead. |
| `allow_duplicate` | boolean | no | Optional, default false — LEAVE UNSET unless you are certain. Starting this template while an execution you coordinate is already in flight is refused as a concurrent double-fire (exec 169/170 incident). Pass true ONLY when a second simultaneous run of the same template is genuinely intended, and say why in the run request. |
